preamble: A glottal stop [ʔ] is inserted to give a vowel-initial syllable an onset or to break up vowel hiatus. Standard German inserts [ʔ] before vowel-initial stems in careful speech. Dutch inserts it between vowels in hiatus, as in beamen [bəˈʔaːmə(n)]. Bohemian Czech uses it at word and morpheme boundaries before a vowel. Malay and Indonesian insert it where a vowel-final prefix or stem meets a vowel. The inserted stop is predictable and usually not written. Cuzco Quechua inserts [ʔ] before an utterance-initial vowel (/ˈaja/ [ˈʔaja] 'corpse').

examples.note: In careful speech a glottal stop occurs before stems beginning with a vowel and before stressed vowels inside a word. It is more frequent in northern varieties and is not treated as a phoneme.
[ʔ] separates /ə/ or /aː/ from a following vowel; it also occurs in compounds such as mee-eten and hippie-ideaal.
Inserted at a morpheme boundary before a vowel; usual in Bohemia, while Moravian speakers say [znɛuʒiːvat].
Inserted at a word boundary between two vowels; also trojúhelník [trojʔuːɦɛlɲiːk] 'triangle'.
A glottal stop is inserted to avoid vowel hiatus at the prefix-stem boundary and is not written.
Inserted when a stem ending in /a/ takes the suffix -an; likewise bacaan [ba.t͡ʃa.ʔan] 'reading'.
A glottal stop is inserted before a vowel at the start of an utterance, but not after a vowel-final word.

sources: Rodríguez Champi, A. (2006). Quechua de Cusco. http://lengamer.org/publicaciones/trabajos/quechua_cusco_afi.pdf
